name: Prime Movers Lab
identity_check: Confirmed as Prime Movers Lab (primemoverslab.com), the breakthrough-science venture firm Dakin Sloss founded in 2018 (team page: Founder & General Partner). Adviser entity is PRIME MOVERS LAB LLC, an SEC exempt reporting adviser (802-114683, CRD 299803). Its Form ADV lists Prime Movers Lab Fund I-III(-A), Prime Movers Growth Fund I(-A) and about 20 single-company '<Company> PML SPV' vehicles. SEC Form Ds for every Prime Movers fund entity name Dakin Sloss. The Humanoid lead is confirmed: Humanoid's 21 July 2026 release says Prime Movers Lab led its $152M Series A, and the firm's homepage and portfolio page list Humanoid. Not the engineering term 'prime mover' (engines/turbines), not PrimeMover-branded equipment or logistics companies, not Prime Ventures (Netherlands) or Prime Venture Partners (India). 'Prime Movers Labs' (TechCrunch 2023) is a misspelling of this firm.

thesis_text.value: Backs inventor-founders commercializing breakthrough science across energy, transportation, infrastructure, manufacturing, human augmentation and agriculture. Started with seed and Series A checks from early-stage funds, then added an early-growth fund and single-company SPVs for later rounds. Deliberately makes few investments and pairs capital with technical diligence, executive coaching, hiring, PR and government-relations help.

open_items: No check size stated on the firm's site, its fund releases or the round announcements fetched.

No application form or pitch URL. The homepage invites founders to 'Contact Us', which links to an obfuscated general info@ mailbox, so application_url is not recorded. Cold inbound is inferred from that invitation.
Nothing found on investing in Indian founders. No stated US-entity requirement: the firm backs UK-based Humanoid and Darmstadt-headquartered Focused Energy, but both have US offices.

No total portfolio count reported. The portfolio page lists 23 current companies and 6 public companies or exits. TechCrunch (2021) reported Fund I invested in 15 companies and Fund II planned about 30.
Fund close dates are the dates the funds were announced, not documented final closes. The Fund II/II-A and Growth Fund I Form Ds are initial notices with no sales reported.

The legal vehicle for the $500M Early Growth Fund isn't confirmed. Form ADV (2026-03-17) lists Prime Movers Growth Fund I LP (gross asset value $1,443,990,518) and Growth Fund I-A LP ($50,357,071), but no page ties them to the announced fund. 'Prime Movers Early Growth Fund III LP' appears only in the combined January 2022 Form D and was dropped in the 2023 amendment.

Prime Movers Fund IV LP (Form D 2026-02-27, organized 2025) and Prime Movers Early Growth Fund II LP (Form D 2026-08-13): indefinite offerings with no sales yet. No announcement, size or close was found. Both list a Miami address.

Form ADV also lists about 20 single-company SPVs, including Halo Industries PML SPV 1-4, Tarana PML SPV 1-2, Commonwealth Fusion Systems, Epirus, Diamond Age, Turntide, Space PML SPV 1 ($94.8M gross asset value) and Paradromics. Round details for these weren't found.

Only 5 of the 9 rounds fall in the last 24 months. Checked, but the announcement doesn't name Prime Movers Lab: Aalo Series B (Aug 2025), Lila Sciences $350M Series A (Oct 2025), Figure Series C (Sept 2025), Atom Computing Series C (June 2026), Commonwealth Fusion $1B raise (July 2026), Pyka $40M Series B (Sept 2024), Quantum Space SPAC/PIPE (June 2026). The Venus Aerospace $91M Series B (July 2026) names Prime Movers Lab only in the boilerplate backer list, so it is not recorded.

Not fetchable (403 or paywall): Forbes Humanoid articles, Reuters Humanoid, Bloomberg Hark, Business Wire originals (Focused Energy, Zafrens), PitchBook Halo Series B. Zafrens' $23M financing led by Prime Movers Lab (Dec 2023) is seen only as a blurb on the firm's news page; stage unknown, not recorded.
Halo Series A: amount not stated, and the $67.5M valuation (pre/post unclear) is left null. Its source is the firm's own summary of a PitchBook article.
HQ and founding year not stated on fetched pages for Hark and The Path. Founding year not stated for Quantum Space, LyGenesis, Lyten and Atom Computing. Hark's Series A amount is 'over $700 million'.
Related party: Tony Robbins is a Prime Movers Lab Partner and co-founder of The Path, whose seed round Prime Movers Lab led.
Former partners named in older releases (Gaetano Crupi, Amy Kruse, Brandon Simmons, David Siminoff, Suzanne Fletcher) are not on the current team page and are not recorded.
